content: For individuals with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD), the selection of glucose-lowering medications should be guided by the risks of CKD progression, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and hypoglycemia. In patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 60 mL/min/1. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) advises careful monitoring of metformin use in patients with an eGFR between 30-45 mL/min/1.73 m². As CKD progresses, metformin use may need to be reduced or discontinued to prevent potential adverse effects, such as lactic acidosis. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are typically recommended in this population due to their demonstrated cardiovascular and renal protective properties.
